subject: MAP: phased commit & monthly TPM cadence discussion
messages:
From: Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@boxbyte.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: lisa.cho@boxbyte.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + evaluation -> proposed commit & ramp

Aisha — thanks again for the demo this week. Per our conversation the execs want a short, measurable MAP tied to commits so we can justify a faster expansion if the eval goes well. My initial draft attached (BoxByte_MAP_v2.pdf). High level: we’re proposing a 6-month evaluation that transitions into a committed plan if we hit the milestones.

Quick summary:
- Month 1 (canary): 250M tokens TPM (proof of concept, latency tests, integrations)
- Month 2–3: ramp to 500M TPM
- Month 4–6: target 1B TPM steady state
- Discount triggers: 10% at sustained 500M TPM for 2 months, 20% at sustained 1B TPM for 2 months

Questions for you:
1) Can Redwood guarantee the same pricing ladder if we sign a 12-month SOW following the trial?
2) Do commits count across subaccounts (we have two product lines)?
3) How does overage billing work if we spike above committed TPM for short periods?

We’ll need a milestone-based invoice schedule (monthly) and a clean mechanism for clawback/credits if you can’t meet latency SLOs during canary.

Attaching: BoxByte_MAP_v2.pdf

—Timothy
Timothy Harris
Head of Platform
BoxByte
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@boxbyte.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + evaluation -> proposed commit & ramp

Timothy — thanks for the clear draft and the MAP attachment. Appreciate the specificity; that makes structuring the ramp easy. A few notes from our side after an initial read:

- Short answer to your questions: yes to counting across subaccounts (we’ll set the aggregation in the MAP), and we can do monthly milestone invoices. Overage treatment: short spikes (<48h) are billed at pro-rated usage with no penalty; longer sustained overages roll into next month unless you want to convert to a higher committed tier.

Proposed adjustments (to keep your early eval low risk):
- Month 1 canary: keep at 250M TPM but we recommend an initial 2-week smoke + 2-week canary cadence (staggered ramp within month 1) so we can tune KV-cache and batching for your typical sequences.
- Discount ladder: we can offer a credit-style mechanism instead of immediate invoice discount. If you sustain 500M TPM for 2 consecutive months we’ll credit 10% of those months’ charges back as account credit; same for 1B TPM at 20%. Credits are applied monthly once the milestone completes.
- SLAs: latency SLOs for canary will be scoped per workload; we’ll include an error-budget credit applied as service credits (not cash) — discuss with legal.

I’ve attached a quick pricing sketch (pricing_model_tpm.csv) that maps token tiers to pro-rated monthly invoices and credit mechanics. If that looks good I’ll ask Ben to draft the SOW/commit language and we’ll circulate for signature.

Next steps I propose:
1) Agree on the ramp schedule (including subaccount aggregation rule) — please confirm if BoxByte wants per-product caps.
2) Agree on credit vs discount mechanics.
3) If agreed, Ben will seed SOW and we’ll aim for signature within 10 business days to lock pricing.

Attachment: pricing_model_tpm.csv

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@boxbyte.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + evaluation -> proposed commit & ramp

Timothy / Aisha — looping in for legal/ops language. A few operational points to make the SOW clean:

- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears with invoice terms Net30. We’ll include a short description of what counts as sustained TPM (rolling 30-day average).
- Commit enforcement: commits are financial (you commit $$$ based on the agreed token rates). If usage is below commit we’ll allow a one-time catch-up within the quarter; otherwise credits are forfeited.
- Overage handling: as Aisha said — brief spikes billed at usage; sustained overages are netted and applied against next month’s commit.
- Early termination: we typically allow a 90-day notice with early termination fee equal to 25% of the remaining committed spend unless there’s a material breach. If BoxByte requires a softer term we can propose a graduated fee schedule tied to milestone completion.

I’ll seed SOW_BoxByte_draft.docx with this language and the credit ladder mechanics. Please review and flag any must-have clauses (e.g., data residency, audit rights).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@boxbyte.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: lisa.cho@boxbyte.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + evaluation -> proposed commit & ramp

Thanks Ben/Aisha — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from procurement before we route to legal:

- Aggregation: BoxByte confirms we want commits counted across both product lines (yes to the subaccount aggregation you described).
- Credits vs immediate invoice discount: Procurement prefers a straight discount applied to invoices (reduces accounting complexity). Is Redwood open to applying the 10%/20% as invoice-level discounts once the tier is reached, rather than account credits?
- Early termination: we’d prefer a graduated early termination fee (12% first 90 days, 6% after 90 days) instead of a flat 25% — on the table?
- SLA/remedy: we need a clarified definition of latency SLOs for canary months (p99 < 600ms for our main endpoint) and a service credit equivalent in dollars for failure to meet that.

If Redwood can accept invoice-level discounts and the softened termination fee, we should be able to route to legal this afternoon. Also please confirm whether the MAP milestones can be captured in HubSpot (we’ll need visibility).

—Timothy
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@boxbyte.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 22:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP + evaluation -> proposed commit & ramp

Timothy — quick confirmation from our side so you can move to legal:

- Aggregation: confirmed — commits will aggregate across subaccounts; we’ll add a short definition in the MAP doc to avoid ambiguity.
- Discount mechanics: we can offer invoice-level discounts (10% at sustained 500M TPM x2 months; 20% at sustained 1B TPM x2 months) instead of credits. We’ll mark discounts as retroactive to the first month that meets the threshold and apply on the invoice following the milestone verification.
- Early termination: we can accept the graduated schedule you proposed (12% in first 90 days, 6% after 90 days) in lieu of the 25% flat fee.
- SLA/remedy: we’ll translate the latency SLO to a numeric p99 target in the SOW (suggest p99 < 650ms for the canary grade; if BoxByte needs 600ms we’ll note that as your “performance target” and attach an explicit dollar-denominated service credit table). Legal will draft the exact remedy language.

Next steps:
1) Ben to upload the seeded SOW (SOW_BoxByte_draft.docx) in the shared drive and push a DocuSign wrapper.
2) I’ll update the MAP PDF to include the aggregation rule and discount ladder and post as final.
3) If you sign the SOW by EOD Friday (2025-07-25) we’ll lock the quoted pricing and the ramp schedule.

Links: https://hubspot.company/record/contacts/12345 (MAP milestones tab)
Draft SOW link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/sow/BX-2025-137

Attachment: SOW_BoxByte_draft.docx (will be uploaded to Drive)

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
